body: Each compares matching elements and gives a logical array: true (1) where the comparison holds. A scalar is compared with every element, and a row with a column makes a matrix. For text, `==` compares character by character and needs the same length: use `strcmp` to compare whole texts. Floating-point results rarely compare equal exactly; compare with a tolerance.
syntax: The same as `A == B`; `ne`, `lt`, `gt`, `le` and `ge` likewise.

pages.summary: Logical AND, OR and NOT element by element: &, | and ~.
body: `A & B` is true where both are nonzero, `A | B` where either is, `~A` where `A` is zero. In an `if` or `while` condition, `&&` and `||` are the short-circuit forms: they evaluate the right side only when they need to, and work on scalars.
syntax: The same as `A & B`; `or(A, B)` and `not(A)` likewise.

pages.summary: Logical exclusive OR: true where exactly one of the two is nonzero.
syntax: True where `A` or `B` is nonzero, but not both.

pages.summary: Like isequal, with NaN equal to NaN.
body: Compares whole arrays as `isequal` does (the same size and the same values), but treats `NaN` values in the same places as equal: useful to compare data with missing values.
syntax: True when every argument equals the first, NaN equal to NaN.

examples.title: Missing values in the same places

pages.summary: Tests for NaN, for infinite values, and for finite values.
body: Element by element. `NaN` is not equal to itself, so `isnan` is the way to find it. `isfinite` is true for numbers that are neither `Inf`, `-Inf` nor `NaN`.

pages.summary: True for missing elements: NaN, <missing> strings, blanks in a char array, empty text in a cell, NaT, undefined categories.
body: What counts as missing depends on the kind of data: `NaN` in numbers, `<missing>` in strings, `NaT` in datetimes, undefined values in categorical arrays, empty text in a cell array of text, and blanks in a character array. For a table, each variable is tested.
syntax: For each element of each variable of a table.
